title: Redwood Discovery - Model selection & deployment options
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
summary: Initial discovery to understand AstraMed's model selection criteria. They need multilingual clinical summarization and question answering with long context (40k+), tool-calling for EMR lookups, and strict security (HIPAA, audit logs). Discussed open models (Llama-3, Mistral, Llama-2 variants), quantization tradeoffs, and deployment options (hosted for fast evals, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private/VPC for HIPAA). Agreed next steps: Redwood to run a benchmark with AstraMed sample docs on 32k/64k context variants, send security pack, and provide Dedicated sizing + pricing.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sofia (AstraMed Head of Data), Ravi (AstraMed ML), Olivia (CTO), Daniel (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): AstraMed is evaluating host vs dedicated vs private for clinical summarization and QA over long patient histories; needs multilingual (EN/ES/PT) + tool calling into EMR; privacy constraints (HIPAA) push them to Private or Dedicated with VPC; requested benchmarks and security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, I'm Maya Chen, account exec for Redwood Inference. we also have Liam and Priya from solutions.
[00:12] Sofia: Hi. Sofia here, thanks. we'll give a quick background and then dive into requirements.
[00:18] Ravi: Hey all. I'm Ravi, ml engineer, will be doing most of the POC work.
[00:22] Olivia: Olivia, CTO. happy to sit in for architecture and compliance questions.
[00:28] Daniel: Daniel, security. will flag anything HIPAA/BAA related.
[00:32] Liam: Great, cool. to frame the convo, we're here to help you pick a model and deployment that balances latency, cost, and PHI controls. can you describe the main product use cases?
[00:45] Sofia: Sure. We do clinical summarization and cohort-level QA for our clinicians. basically pull together patient histories from EMR — notes, labs, imaging reports — and present a one-page summary and answer clinician questions. average token window per patient is large, like 25k to 50k tokens depending on history.
[01:08] Maya: 25k to 50k, got it. is that raw text or after some extraction?
[01:14] Sofia: raw text. we do some light cleaning but keep most of the notes. also we need Spanish and Portuguese support for certain clinics.
[01:22] Liam: ok multilingual + long context. good to know. and tool-calling? you mentioned EMR lookups — is that live function calling integrated?
[01:30] Ravi: yes, we want the model to be able to call our EMR API to fetch structured lab history when prompted and then synthesize. so function / tool calling support is a must.
[01:40] Maya: Great. on the security side? HIPAA concerns?
[01:44] Daniel: Absolutely. Data residency and BAA are required. audit logs, KMS for key management, retention controls, and SSO/SAML. Also we want fine-grained RBAC so non-clinical users can't access PHI outputs.
[01:58] Priya: That's all supported across our Dedicated and Private options; Hosted can be used for early evals with stricter contractual controls but for production HIPAA we'd typically look at Dedicated or Private.
[02:12] Olivia: curious on performance: latency targets for clinicians are low — ideally <2s per token for interactive Q&A and sub-500ms for embeddings lookup. is that realistic?
[02:24] Liam: depends on model and deployment. with Dedicated on A100s or H100s and optimized kernels, we can get interactive latencies. but for 32k/64k context models there's tradeoffs. we can use KV cache and prefix caching to keep latency reasonable.
[02:40] Sofia: On models, we've been testing Llama-2 and a few open models from HF but we saw quality drift on clinical prompts. any recommendations?
[02:52] Liam: clinically, we've seen Llama-3 family perform better on instruction tuning; Mistral is also strong but sometimes struggles on specific medical terminology. Llama-2 iso variants can be cheaper, though older. For long context, there are 32k and 64k context variants — Llama-3-32k, Llama-3-64k, Mistral-32k (experimental 64k via chunking). Quantization (4-bit/8-bit) helps cost but can impact subtle clinical accuracy — we should benchmark.
[03:18] Ravi: Does Redwood support function/tool calling reliably for these open models or is that a hosted wrapper?
[03:26] Priya: We have a function-calling interface at the API layer that works regardless of model, but some models need small adapter code to make deterministic structured outputs. for model-native function calling (like schema enforcement) we add an output-parser layer.
[03:40] Daniel: network & keys: if we go Dedicated or Private, how do you handle KMS and HSM?
[03:46] Maya: For Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS over customer-managed keys (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via PKCS11 for Private deployments). audit logs are exported to your SIEM and we offer per-call metadata.
[04:00] Olivia: and, do you support bringing your own model? we might want to run a specialized clinical model internally.
[04:06] Liam: Yes, BYOM is possible in Dedicated and Private. We can host customer models if licensing permits. Redwood also offers a model catalog with vetted variants.
[04:16] Sofia: Ok, important: context length — can you do 64k with fast enough throughput for clinicians? if we need 64k we don't want 10s latencies.
[04:27] Liam: 64k is doable but cost and latency scale. strategies: 1) use a 64k native context model (higher VRAM), 2) do intelligent retrieval + chunking and KV caching so only delta tokens are processed each turn. For interactive UX we often combine retrieval-augmented generation with prefix caching. We'll show numbers in the benchmark.
[04:48] Ravi: On multilingual, do any models degrade a lot? our Spanish prompts are clinical and often include colloquial shorthand from notes.
[04:56] Liam: Llama-3 has better multilingual coverage than Llama-2 in our tests, Mistral also OK but Spanish clinical shorthand is tricky — we can fine-tune or do RL fine-tuning or few-shot prompt tuning. For POC, prompts + curated eval set show big differences.
[05:12] Sofia: can we run small fine-tuning or LoRA in Dedicated?
[05:16] Priya: Yes, we support LoRA and parameter-efficient tuning on Dedicated and Private. Hosted has limited fine-tune options currently.
[05:24] Olivia: pricing and sizing question: if we wanted Dedicated — what's the expected footprint for steady state 50 concurrent short Q&A sessions with 32k context?
[05:33] Liam: rough back-of-envelope: 50 concurrent 32k context interactive sessions likely need a few multi-GPU nodes — depends on model and batching. we can size with trace data; we'll do a capacity estimate in the follow-up.
[05:45] Sofia: also we need function-calls to be auditable — who called what and what triggered a call. can we log that?
[05:52] Maya: yes, we include per-call metadata, function-call events, and structured logs for retrace. these can be exported through syslog or S3.
[06:00] Daniel: retention & deletion policies? Need ability to purge patient data on request within X days and restrict retention in staging environments.
[06:08] Priya: retention controls are configurable in Dedicated/Private; Hosted can be negotiated. we support auto-purge and hard-delete APIs plus retention TTLs.
[06:16] Ravi: For the benchmark, we want you to test Llama-3-32k, Llama-3-64k, and Mistral-32k quantized to 4-bit; measure latency P50/P95, cost tokens, and clinical accuracy on our QA set.
[06:30] Liam: sounds good. we'll run quantized and FP16 baselines. any specific accuracy metric?
[06:36] Sofia: Prefer F1 on entity extraction and clinician-rated summary quality (1-5) on 200 samples. We'll provide guidance.
[06:44] Maya: Great. we'll need samples and an EMR API spec for the tool-calling test.
[06:49] Ravi: I'll send redacted samples and an API swagger doc.
[07:00] -- (audio gap, cough) --
[07:20] Sofia: quick question — do you support streaming partial responses during long summarizations? clinicians like to see progressive output.
[07:28] Priya: yes, streaming is supported for hosted and Dedicated. for Private we can enable streaming via the local gateway. streaming behavior differs slightly with prefix caching but it is supported.
[07:40] Olivia: any known failure modes when combining streaming+function-calls?
[07:45] Liam: worst is inconsistent partial outputs if function-calls fire mid-stream; we buffer function calls and have deterministic commit points. we can demo this in POC.
[07:56] Daniel: about SSO - we use SAML and SCIM. integration complexity?
[08:01] Maya: Supported; we do SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user RBAC.
[08:06] Sofia: What about model drift detection and evals? we want to monitor hallucinations and accuracy over time.
[08:12] Priya: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring tied to eval sets and prompt sets; it can alert on regressions and snapshot model outputs. we'll include that in docs.
[08:24] Ravi: competitor question — we tried hosted Vertex endpoints; the latency there for 32k was really bad. how do you compare?
[08:32] Liam: we publish per-model perf profiles; Dedicated tends to beat generic managed endpoints because of kernel selection, batching and KV cache. we'll share benchmark sheets.
[08:42] Olivia: licensing — if we use Llama-3 or Mistral, any legal issues?
[08:48] Maya: we'll surface license terms; BYOM requires you ensure license compliance. we can help with license text if needed.
[08:56] Sofia: ok moving to next steps and recap.
[09:00] Maya: recap: 1) Redwood to run benchmark on provided samples for Llama-3-32k, Llama-3-64k, Mistral-32k quantized 4-bit and FP16 baselines measuring latency and quality. 2) Send security / HIPAA docs and KMS/HSM integration notes. 3) AstraMed to share redacted patient samples and EMR API. 4) schedule follow-up week of Dec 15.
[09:20] Olivia: sounds good. any other questions?
[09:24] Daniel: one last — does Redwood offer BAAs?
[09:28] Maya: Yes; we'll include BAA language and customer references for healthcare.
[09:33] Ravi: timeline — we want POC running by early Jan if the benchmarks look good.
[09:38] Priya: we'll prioritize the benchmark and aim for results by Dec 14.
[09:42] Sofia: thanks. we'll send samples by Dec 9.
[09:46] Olivia: thanks everyone.
[09:48] -- end of recording --
